Okay, first. Biological immortals - the Centurions. A group of powerful human beings who, thanks to a number of scientific innovations, cannot age. They can still die, so they aren't necessarily immortal, but they are immortal in that they live forever. Of course, by the time the main story takes place, most of them are dead, but that's irrelevant to this question.

As for Gods, there are two main godlike beings in my world - the first(though I hesitate to order them first and second) are the Sentinels of Dawn, mechanized warriors cast in the early dawn of Time to protect and serve the Empire. Eons after the it has faded away into disexistence, they still stand guard, waiting for the day when the heir returns to bring the Empire back to it's former glory.

The second is an oddity - they are, quite simply, the Past, Present, and Future, manifested as physical entities. It's weird - I know, but the way it ties into the story works it out to be a pretty cool concept.

I can see a few additional conflicts arising in this season as well.

I can see a conflict forming between Bellamy and Octavia in regards to Echo. Octavia banished her with the full intent of having her die out there, so I imagine finding out that she's not only alive, but that Bellamy trusts and likely cares for her will create a huge rift between her. 

I can also see conflicts arising in the bunker. Based on all we've seen of the grounders in the past four seasons, I cannot see them abandoning their clan rivalries. Indra herself said without a leader the clans wouldn't unite, and I can't see them leading well for 6 years on limited resources, especially for the grounder clans. Skaikru will be fine - they've been through it all before and worse, but the grounders (from what we've seen) have never dealt with this kind of situation. Because of this, I can see Skaikru acting as mediators between the clans, as they know how hard it is to live like the Bunkerkru are living, but they also know it's possible to survive it. I can see Kane leading this.

I can see this conflict being amplified when Spacekru and Bunkerkru are reunited with each other and back out on the surface fighting for food/land in the tiny patch of livable land. I can also see Echo playing into this (which is part of why I think they made her a regular). Echo was an Ice Nation spy and is likely the highest member of their chain of command left alive. Grounders love tradition, so I can see the Ice Nation clan and their allies, if they have any, looking towards Echo as a leader. Echo can either join them or be like "y'all I just spent 6 years getting baked up in space, I'll pass on your dumbass fight." 

I can also, of course, see a conflict between the Bunkerkru/Spacekru and Miningkru. As I've mentioned before in other threads, I think nightblood will play a big role in this. The show's never really tackled racism, and I can see it being a theme of the next season.

As for Clarke, I feel like her conflicts won't really be with Spacekru or Bunkerkru too much, and instead will focus more on the conflict with the Spacekru. I think they've gone to war. A few reasons for it.

1) We don't know the size of the bunker. All we know is that it can hold at least 1200 people, but it could easily be more. The writers have a lot of wiggle room there.

2) The grounders aren't used to those conditions. They've never, from what we've seen, had to deal with rationing or cramped living quarters. Never had to deal with limited supplies like they will be.

3) The group is pissed and in power. The group is the only one that knows how to operate the bunker, but they're also reasonably pissed because 300 of their own were killed after they had already all been safe, even if how they got to be safe was illegitimate.

4) A specific character. A showrunner has said in interviews she'll be in a place people don't expect, but I think there were a few hints to it in her last conversation with another character. a) The girl under the floor and b) A specific reference. Both, obviously, references to the first season, but given the "reset" that the fifth season will be, I can see them being a hint of things to come for her.

5) Another character. They made her actor a regular for a reason, and I don't think it was availability concerns like was no doubt the reason another character became one. She is, at the end of the fourth season, a banished scout/spy. I think both of these things will come into play. Her banishment, obviously, will cause conflict with two other characters. Both of them never expected her to live, so seeing her alive after 6 years and more importantly seeing her with the male lead and probably pretty close to him will piss them both off. Likewise, her position as one of the only surviving commander types will come into play with the grounder conflict I anticipate. Her former faction and their allies will likely ask her to lead them, and she either gives them the finger and goes with the male lead, or she betrays him. I would obviously prefer the latter option, but I can see them pulling the former. At the very least I expect her to be conflicted no matter what choice she makes.
